ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Feeling hot (possible heat intolerance) and severe intermittent headaches.
• Symptom details:
  – Headaches: Frontal, severe, come and go, mainly during working hours while on laptop or in meetings; began after changing jobs; mild nausea occasionally; no radiation.
  – Palpitations: Sense of fast-beating heart, ~1×/day, sometimes noted in elevator and at desk.
  – Shortness of breath: Episodic, occurs while sitting at desk, not with exercise.
  – Paresthesias: Tingling in both arms ("quick pricking"), no leg involvement.
  – Constitutional / other: Reduced appetite, unintentional 5-lb weight loss, feeling hot, loss of libido.
• Onset/duration: All symptoms started after starting new job (exact timeframe not specified; presumed weeks–months).
• Aggravating factors: Work stress, computer/meeting time. No clear relieving factors reported.
• Past medical history: Thyroid disease (patient states "hyper-thyroidism" but is taking thyroxine – suggests treated hypothyroidism).
• Medications: Thyroxine (dose not specified).
• Allergies: None reported.
• Social history: Lawyer in London; job stress rated 7–8/10. Alcohol: couple of glasses of wine once/week. Non-smoker. No recreational drugs.
• Family history: Not discussed in transcript.
• Vital signs / physical exam: None obtained in tele-visit.
• Labs / imaging: None yet performed (doctor plans thyroid studies and general blood work).

V: Essential hypertension with episodic hypertensive surges: Could cause frontal headaches and palpitations, though no BP readings available.
Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia: Palpitations and light-headedness could produce tingling and SOB.
I: Viral upper-respiratory or systemic infection: Could give fevers/"feeling hot" and headaches, but other systemic signs absent.
N: Intracranial mass lesion (e.g., brain tumor): Can cause new severe headaches, nausea, weight loss, libido changes.
D: Tension-type or cervicogenic headache related to prolonged computer use and posture; stress exacerbated.
Vitamin B12 deficiency: Can cause paresthesias, fatigue, appetite change.
I2: Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism from excess thyroxine replacement: Heat intolerance, weight loss, palpitations, anxiety, decreased libido.
Caffeine overuse (common in law professionals): Can produce headaches, palpitations, tremor/paresthesias.
C: Congenital cardiac conduction disorder causing arrhythmias and palpitations – less likely given adult onset.
A: Graves disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism): Same symptom constellation; possible if thyroid status has shifted.
T: None apparent – no trauma history linked to onset.
E: Generalized anxiety / panic disorder (stress-related endocrine–autonomic response): Explains headaches, palpitations, SOB, paresthesias, appetite & libido loss.
Hyperthyroidism (endocrine overactivity whether exogenous or endogenous).

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism due to excessive thyroxine replacement
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: The patient is on thyroxine and reports multiple classic hyper-thyroid symptoms (heat intolerance, weight loss, palpitations, decreased libido, anxiety-like symptoms). Dose may be too high or requirement may have fallen, leading to biochemical hyperthyroidism.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Stress-related / anxiety or panic disorder with tension-type headaches
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: New highly stressful job; symptoms cluster during work, include headaches, palpitations, SOB and arm tingling that can all be produced by hyperventilation and autonomic arousal. Weight and libido changes also common.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Primary tension or migraine headaches exacerbated by screen work
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Frontal, severe headaches during computer use; mild nausea suggests migraine component; lack of prior headache history supports new primary headache triggered by work ergonomics/stress.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Endogenous hyperthyroidism (Graves disease or toxic multinodular goitre)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Same symptom profile as #1 but would represent disease progression rather than medication excess. Possible if patient mislabeled diagnosis or is non-adherent/over-supplemented.
New severe headaches and weight loss could signal a mass, but episodic nature tied to work and presence of autonomic symptoms make it less likely.

supporting_opposing.diagnosis: Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism due to excessive thyroxine replacement
supporting_evidence: Unintentional weight loss despite reduced appetite
opposing_evidence: No tremor, diarrhea, or overt goitre reported
Duration unclear; symptoms fluctuate with work (could fit anxiety)

Loss of appetite and libido common in chronic stress
opposing_evidence: Objective weight loss and heat intolerance less typical
No explicit report of feeling anxious or panicked

supporting_evidence: Frontal severe headaches with mild nausea
No prior history – new environmental trigger
opposing_evidence: Does not explain palpitations, SOB, tingling, weight loss
Headaches not described as throbbing or photophobic

supporting_evidence: Same symptom triad as iatrogenic hyperthyroidism
